title: Refactor a 300-line Python script
persona: Dhruv, summer intern at a startup
scenario: Your manager dropped a 300-line Python script that scrapes data, cleans it, and emails a daily report. It works. It's also one giant function with 11 nested if-statements, prints used as logs, and credentials hard-coded at line 12. You have 2 days to refactor before the next intern inherits it. You want the refactor to teach the next person what the code does, not just make it shorter.
badOutput: I'll help you refactor your script. General refactoring tips: break into functions, use logging instead of print, move credentials to environment variables, add type hints, write docstrings. Without seeing the code, I can give general guidance.

hints.title: Name the actual smells
hints.body: Call out the 11 nested ifs, the prints-as-logs, and hard-coded credentials. Specific smells beat ‘refactor this code’.

hints.title: Force a teaching motive
hints.body: ‘Refactor so the next intern can learn from it, not just so it's shorter.’ This changes how AI structures comments and module boundaries.

checks.tip: Anchor the language and shape, Python script.
Anchor the scale and shape, 300 lines, 11 nested ifs.
Surface the credentials issue, that's a security smell.
Name the audience, the next intern. Forces clarity.
Force the teaching motive, not ‘make it shorter’.
Demand testability as a refactor goal.
Demand a module/function breakdown, not a single file.
Demand before/after or annotated rationale per change.

tipIfLow: Refactor prompts get generic because they say ‘refactor this’ without naming the smells. The unlock is naming specific smells (11 nested ifs, prints-as-logs, hard-coded creds) AND a teaching motive (‘so the next intern can learn’). Refactor for the human downstream.
goldPrompt: Act as a senior reviewer mentoring a junior. I'm Dhruv, summer intern. I have 2 days to refactor a 300-line Python script before another intern inherits it. Smells: one giant function, 11 nested if-statements, prints used as logs, hard-coded credentials at line 12. The refactor goal is TEACHING the next person, not minimising lines. Output: (1) the refactored module breakdown with names + responsibilities, (2) one-line description of what each file contains, (3) the 3 hardest decisions you faced and the trade-off, (4) what you'd flag as 'leave a comment for next intern'. Don't print code blocks longer than 20 lines.
